extracted.intended_audience: journalists and newsroom leaders interested in trauma reporting
extracted.subtask_description: A concise organizational overview of the Dart Center for Journalism and Trauma, its mission, programs, fellowships, and activities designed to improve ethical reporting and support journalists who cover violence, conflict and tragedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: improve quality of journalism on traumatic events
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dart Center's mission was to improve the quality of journalism on traumatic events, while also raising awareness in newsrooms of the impact such coverage has on the journalists telling the stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames evaluation of reporting on trauma by dual criteria: (1) the substantive quality of coverage of traumatic events, and (2) attention to the wellbeing and secondary effects on the journalists producing that coverage. Use both journalistic standards (accuracy, context, ethical treatment of victims) and newsroom practices (support, debriefing, training) when judging adherence to this mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nurture innovation in ethical reporting on victims of violence and tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dart Center was founded to nurture innovation in ethical reporting on victims of violence and tragedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes development and promotion of new ethical approaches and practices in reporting about victims. Evaluation should look for adoption of novel methods that protect victim dignity, minimize retraumatization, and balance public interest with compassion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship eligibility and purpose (Ochberg Fellowship)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship program, called after Frank Ochberg, is aimed at mid career journalists who want to deepen their knowledge of emotional trauma and improve coverage of violence, conflict and tragedy; six to ten journalists are selected every year to attend an intensive weeklong seminar program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection criteria implied: mid-career status, demonstrated interest in deepening trauma knowledge, and a commitment to improving coverage. The program structure (weeklong seminar, peer discussion, conference participation) signals expected outcomes: enhanced subject-matter understanding and practical newsroom improvements. Use these elements to evaluate applicants or similar fellowship designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide seminars, training and support programs for journalists covering traumatic events
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dart Center conducted seminars, training and support programs for journalists covering the attacks of September 11, 2001, Hurricane Katrina, the Boxing Day tsunami, the Troubles in Northern Ireland, the Iraq War and the Virginia Tech shootings, among other events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic evaluation should consider whether trainings are event-specific or generalizable, include psychological support components, and address both reporting techniques and reporter wellbeing. Examples of major events illustrate scope and types of curricula to model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and lead research on psychological impact of reporting traumatic events
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dart Center encouraged and led research on the psychological impact of reporting traumatic events on journalists, and encouraged the development of training and support programs at leading news organizations around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards include commissioning empirical research into reporter mental health, translating findings into training, and advocating for institutional adoption. Evaluation of an organization should check for active research, published findings, and evidence of uptake by news organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and implement newsroom peer support programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Dart Centre Asia Pacific worked actively ... pioneering newsroom peer support programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for newsroom practice: existence of peer support mechanisms (trained peers, debrief protocols, referral pathways). Assessments should look for documented programs, training for peer supporters, and integration into newsroom workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate regional centers and research nodes to extend reach
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dart Center also operated Dart Centre Europe, based in London; Dart Centre Asia Pacific, based in Melbourne; and a research node at the University of Tulsa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational best practice implied: maintain regional presences to tailor training and support across jurisdictions and cultures. Evaluation can consider geographic coverage, local partnerships, and region-specific programming as markers of capacity and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use awards and conferences to promote excellence and knowledge-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the Dart Center's programs were the annual Dart Center Awards for Excellence in Reporting on Trauma and the annual conference of the International Society for Traumatic Stress Studies (included in fellowship activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for influence include running recognition programs to incentivize high-quality trauma reporting and leveraging professional conferences for dissemination and networking. Evaluate whether awards criteria and conference engagements meaningfully shape reporting standards.
